conventions.convention: n ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ r < n. Hermitian eigenvalues are ordered increasingly with multiplicity; the occupied projector selects the lowest r eigenvalues and is defined only at a strict rth gap. Repeated eigenvalues within either cluster are allowed.
Admissible densities are Hermitian positive contractions with trace r; idempotence is not required. Distances use the Frobenius norm.
The separating circle is positively oriented, centered at λ₁(H₀), with radius (λᵣ(H₀)+λᵣ₊₁(H₀))/2−λ₁(H₀). Perturbation radii and resolvent bounds use the operator norm.
Contraction requires a self-map of a nonempty complete invariant metric space and 0 ≤ q < 1. Set q⁰ = 1, including q = 0; sums at k = 0 are empty.
DIIS coefficients are real, sum to one, and have ℓ¹ norm at most C ≥ 1. Among global least-squares minimizers, select the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm vector, including singular Gram cases.

Safeguarded DIIS accepts a candidate only after K-membership, gap, response-error and fixed-point residual certificates succeed. Its residual upper bound includes the additive response-evaluation error.
Relaxed mixing allows α ∈ [0,1] and tests the relaxed-map residual. At α = 0 that residual is zero without certifying an unmixed SCF fixed point.
Finite-budget loops enter indices 0 through N, test the current residual before the budget return, and update only below N. Termination assumes returning primitives.

load_bearing.statement: For every X ∈ U at which the response map has a strict rth gap, Φ(X) is a uniquely defined member of Pᵣ. Degeneracies among the first r eigenvalues or among the remaining eigenvalues do not affect it.

A q-contraction Φ:K→K on a nonempty complete metric space has a unique fixed point X*. Exact iterates satisfy d(Xₖ,X*) ≤ qᵏd(X₀,X*); d(X,X*) ≤ d(X,Φ(X))/(1−q). Inexact updates in K with error at most ηₖ satisfy eₖ₊₁ ≤ qeₖ+ηₖ and eₖ ≤ qᵏe₀+Σⱼ<ₖqᵏ⁻¹⁻ʲηⱼ.

For H₀ with occupied gap g > 0, its specified circle separates exactly the lowest r eigenvalues of every Hermitian H with ‖H−H₀‖op ≤ g/4; the gap is at least g/2, the contour-to-spectrum distance is at least g/4, and the resolvent norm is at most 4/g.
On ‖H−H₀‖op < g/4, the occupied block projector is real Fréchet C¹ in Frobenius norm, with DΠᵣ(H)[E] = (1/(2πi))∫Γ(zI−H)⁻¹E(zI−H)⁻¹dz and ‖DΠᵣ(H)[E]‖F ≤ (16R/g²)‖E‖F.
For s ≥ 1, same-shaped complex matrices R₁,…,Rₛ and C ≥ 1, J(c)=‖ΣcᵢRᵢ‖F² attains a minimum subject to Σcᵢ=1 and Σ|cᵢ|≤C. Among all minimizers there is a unique vector of minimum Euclidean norm.
For n ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ r < n, Dᵣ is nonempty, closed, and convex in Hₙ, and complete in the Frobenius metric.

On its complete invariant projector set with certified contraction factor q and initial error budget E₀, accept a certified DIIS candidate only when its residual upper bound divided by 1−q is at most qEₖ; otherwise use the certified baseline response and update the budget to qEₖ+η(Pₖ).

seams_checked.note: Read the supplier page and alg-fixed-point-iteration. The SCF algorithms preserve its current-residual-before-budget stopping order and finite update pattern, adding explicit spectral failure branches. They do not import Newton convergence or infer convergence from the iteration interface.

Read the supplier page, projector-domain definition, finite-basis energy-model definition and Hermitian eigenvalue perturbation lemma. The C¹ corollary retains the real C² functional and real-linear interaction hypotheses. Both finite-model examples satisfy self-adjointness of G. The ascending eigenvalue convention explicitly reverses the supplier lemma's descending indices. No minimizer or lowest-occupied ordering is inferred from commutation alone.
